clue.text: Go after funds to take in United

indicators.note: the purse is said to take in, or enclose, the next piece

parts.note: a purse is a sum of money, funds
U is the usual abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football club chases money to sign up a United player.
explanation.definitionFit: To chase or follow something is to go after it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Showing off, scrapping knight with maiden and model

indicators.note: scrapping says the knight is thrown out of the word

parts.note: parading means showing off
N is the chess notation for knight
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A knight is dropped from a parade, alongside a maiden and a model.
explanation.definitionFit: A paradigm is a pattern or exemplar, a model to follow.

clue.text: Gunners parachuting? Bit of a shower

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners
parachuting is arriving in a drop, so in drop

explanation.surface: Artillerymen falling from the sky like a bit of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: One drop of water is a small part of a shower of rain.

clue.text: University can upset this group

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a tin is a can

explanation.surface: The university may disturb this team.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit is a single grouping of people, like a military unit.

clue.text: Good man joins other ranks backing ruler — it's touching

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated St, is a good man

indicators.note: backing here means going backwards, so the other ranks abbreviation is read in reverse

parts.note: OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks, the non-officers
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: A saintly man joins the troops in supporting their monarch, and it moves us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns OR into RO; 'joins' and 'it's' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Caressing with the hand is a form of touching, so the participles match.

clue.text: Crooked attorney sure to make legal tender?

indicators.note: crooked suggests the letters of the two words are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A dishonest lawyer is certain to produce some money?
explanation.definitionFit: A Treasury note was banknote currency issued by the Treasury.

clue.text: Bellows, losing head in rows

indicators.note: losing head says the first letter goes

parts.note: roars means bellows, as a verb

explanation.surface: Someone shouting loses their temper during arguments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' looks like quarrels, but it is the verb for propelling a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To row a boat is to propel it with paddles, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Reformed ladies show the highest standards

indicators.note: reformed means the letters of ladies are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Women who have changed their ways display the loftiest morals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideals are principles of perfection, the loftiest standards one aims for.

clue.text: He's after fuel cuts

indicators.note: after places the he's piece behind the fuel

parts.note: gas is a fuel
the contraction is taken as its letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: He is going after fuel price cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: Gashes are deep wounds or slashes, that is, cuts.

clue.text: Producing endless dried fruit

indicators.note: endless says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: raising, as in raising a family or crops, means producing

explanation.surface: Making a never-ending supply of dried fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried grape is the classic example of dried fruit.

clue.text: Look smaller, though unique

parts.note: to peer is to look closely
less means smaller in amount

explanation.surface: Something appears smaller yet is one of a kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no equal makes a thing unrivalled, so the synonym holds.

clue.text: One will provide care for a small charge

definitions.text: One will provide care for a small charge

parts.words: One will provide care for a small charge
parts.note: charge means a ward, a child in one's care, not a low fee

explanation.surface: Someone offering caring services cheaply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a small charge' reads as a little fee, but it is a young person placed in one's care.
explanation.definitionFit: Such a guardian raises a child who is not their own by birth.

clue.text: Failed Eastern hombre

parts.note: a dud is a failure, so dud as an adjective means failed

explanation.surface: A Spanish-speaking man from the East who failed.
explanation.definitionFit: Hombre is Spanish-flavoured slang for a man or guy, as is the American word.

clue.text: Wood works in church

indicators.note: in places the works inside the church

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
ops, short for opera, are musical works

explanation.surface: Woodwork being carried out inside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A copse is a small thicket of trees, a little wood.

clue.text: A shade too near the knuckle?

definitions.meaning: a colour, as navy or sky
risqué or indecent, as a smutty joke is

explanation.surface: Is this colour a touch too close to bone?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Near the knuckle' is a British idiom for close to being indecent.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a colour and also means smutty, as in a dirty film.

clue.text: Climbing frame — for ramblers?

parts.note: not a playground frame but steps that walkers climb over a field fence

explanation.surface: A playground climbing frame meant for hikers.
explanation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps for crossing a fence or wall, common on British footpaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Walkers clamber over this wooden structure to cross field boundaries.

clue.text: Column seen in flight

parts.note: flight means a flight of stairs, not air travel; the column is the post at its end

explanation.surface: A pillar spotted while flying.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the central or end post of a staircase, supporting the handrail.

clue.text: Spirited relations

parts.note: relations here means narrations, and spirited means about spirits or phantoms, not lively relatives

explanation.surface: Lively members of the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' reads as relatives, but it means tellings of tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Tales of hauntings are narratives featuring spirits.

clue.text: Suddenly stop leading? Time to get your skates on

definitions.meaning: to freeze is to stop suddenly, and up means ahead or in the lead

definitions.text: Time to get your skates on
definitions.meaning: the season when water turns to ice, ready for skating

explanation.surface: The front-runner suddenly halts; time to hurry up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get your skates on' is a British idiom for hurry, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze-up is a period of hard frost when lakes and rivers ice over.

clue.text: Former vicar in holy surroundings

indicators.note: in places the vicar inside the holy surroundings

parts.note: pious means holy or devout
Rev, short for Reverend, is a vicar's title

explanation.surface: An ex-vicar is encircled by devout people.
explanation.definitionFit: Previous means earlier or prior, as a former job is.

clue.text: Frowning with alarm — no time to reveal obvious mistake

parts.note: glaring means scowling or frowning

indicators.note: no time says the abbreviation for time is removed

parts.note: terror is great alarm

explanation.surface: Someone scowls in fright, revealing a blatant blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: Glaring means conspicuous, and an error is a mistake.

clue.text: Reduced fare for buffet users?

parts.note: not a cheap ticket but small portions of food eaten at a buffet or snack bar

explanation.surface: A discount ticket for people using the train buffet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' reads as a ticket price, but it means food; reduced means small.
explanation.definitionFit: Light bites are smaller portions of food, often served at a buffet.

clue.text: A sweet's served up in layers

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means brought upwards, so read in reverse

parts.note: tarts are sweets, desserts, and the s adds the plural

explanation.surface: A dessert is brought up in tiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Strata are layers, especially of rock or sediment.

clue.text: A B C D F or G

definitions.text: A B C D F or G

parts.words: A B C D F or G
parts.note: each letter names a musical pitch, and the run from A to G skips only E

explanation.surface: A list of letters, like grades on a report card.
explanation.walkthrough: Every listed letter is a musical pitch, and the one gap in the run A to G is E, so the answer splits as NOT E.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the letters names a musical pitch in the scale.

clue.text: Change of heart for space traveller

indicators.note: a change of the word heart means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An astronaut has a change of heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet travels through space in orbit around the sun.

clue.text: Lorry driver

parts.note: not a trucker but the fuel that drives a lorry, British diesel

explanation.surface: A man who drives a truck.
explanation.walkthrough: DERV is the British name for diesel fuel for road vehicles; a lorry is a truck.
explanation.definitionFit: Diesel powers, and so drives, heavy goods vehicles.

clue.text: Lower section of natural river

indicators.note: the lower section of the word natural holds the answer in its later letters

explanation.surface: The lower stretch of a river in its natural state.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ural is a river flowing from Russia through Kazakhstan.

clue.text: One's used to travel and is in Virginia

indicators.note: in places is inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: A traveller in Virginia is used to moving around.
explanation.definitionFit: A visa is the passport endorsement needed for entry to many countries.

clue.text: Rickshaw operators who run the business?

definitions.meaning: men who carry or pull a chair-like passenger vehicle

explanation.surface: Rickshaw pullers who also manage the company?
explanation.walkthrough: Chairmen once carried sedan chairs, and the word stretches to those pulling rickshaws.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both chair carriers and those presiding over a company board.

clue.text: He spoke famously of Circe corrupting love

indicators.note: corrupting tells us the name Circe is distorted into a new order

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A man gave a famous speech about the sorceress Circe spoiling love.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman statesman was among history's most celebrated orators.

clue.text: Tries to consume the whole vegetables

indicators.note: the tries eat up, or contain, the whole

parts.note: shots are attempts or tries
all means the whole

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to eat every vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: These small onion relatives are vegetables used in cooking.

clue.text: Pitch a tent on American college grounds

parts.note: to camp is to pitch a tent
US means American

explanation.surface: Students put up a tent on the university lawn in the States.
explanation.definitionFit: The campus is the land and buildings of a college or university.
